title: Prescribed large-volume charges on threefolds with trivial canonical bundle
main_claim: (Thm 1.1) On any smooth projective threefold with K_X trivial, for B and H in open neighbourhoods and t ≥ T (one threshold), two things hold: (Z_{B,tH}, A_{B,tH}) is a geometric stability condition with the standard double-tilt heart and full numerical support, and the square-root-Todd charge Z^LV also admits such a stability condition. (Thm 1.2) On any smooth projective threefold with H integral ample and B0 rational, there are k and R_* that do not depend on E or b, such that ch3^B ≤ (a²/6 + k) H²ch1^B for slope-zero tilt-semistable objects at every a, and the uncorrected BMT inequality holds for a > R_*. (Cor 1.3) This gives a parabolic region where Q_{α,β} ≥ 0.

issues.location: Sec. 6, Lemma 6.2 (elliptic scaled support) and Prop. 6.3 (weighted ambient)
issues.description: The uniform-in-volume ambient support bound rests on external results that I could not check against their sources: the Liu product coefficient condition η ≤ w/C², the uniqueness theorem of ProductsCurves2025 (Thm 3.11) used to identify the slicings from different induction orders, and the LiEtAl2026 and Cheng2026 finite-flat descent, twist-distance and real-weight extension statements. The internal rescaling algebra is consistent: the R-powers cancel in the form q_r, the kernel of the summed form is definite, and the block-pullback comparison (6.?) has R-independent constants. This is a dependency caveat, not an identified gap.
issues.evidence: Proof of Lemma 6.2 cites [LiuProduct2021, Lemma 5.7], [ProductsCurves2025, Thm 3.11/4.5] and [LiEtAl2026, Lemma 6.6]. Prop 6.3 cites [Cheng2026, Prop 4.3, Rem 4.4] and [LiEtAl2026, Prop 3.21, 5.1].

coverage:
Read all of Sections 1–7 line by line and skimmed Section 8. Checks made:
- Sec 6: Knum injectivity under the product embedding; the GRR correction γ = td(Y)(1 − δ/12 or δ/24), which reproduces exactly Z_{B,tH} and Z^LV; the scaled deformation estimate and the Q_t argument for Bayer's deformation theorem; the Bayer-property and truncation hypotheses of the restriction criterion (n1 = −dim Y, n2 = 0, N > dim Y + 1); point stability via primitivity.
- Sec 7: the surface charge's imaginary part tH·(c1 − (B + L/2)r); the section phase inequalities; the weighted slope bounds ±c; B ⊂ P(−1,1]; the phase-one lemma; the zero-denominator lemma; both torsion-pair inclusions in Prop 7.7.
- Sec 3: Langer variance normalisation (h²r²ξ); Nash/Kato heat bounds; the CLR-type matrix spectral bound (the B_≤/B_> split and the HS computation p²/η); the Nakano/Weitzenböck argument giving h¹ ≤ C r ξ; the hull-length identity; the surface Riemann–Roch formula.
- Sec 4: slope bounds b ± A for V and Ū; the excess decompositions and the O(e) bounds on residuals and tails; the line-quotient numerator inequality and the choice of m0; the side point (b − c, √(A² − c²)); every step of the restriction-image lemma (moment bounds on K', h² and χ on S, the cancellation of N, removal of the twist m); the Frobenius presentation and Hom-injectivity; the duality identity for h²; the ramp/Riemann-sum computation giving h r (μ − b)³/6 + C_A r δ; the bound (A+s)³ − A²(A+s) ≤ C_A s; the Adams-operation Riemann–Roch limit; the reduction from negative rank via the dual.
- Sec 5: the derivatives D' and S' along the zero branch; all three comparison functions and the constants R0 and k0; superadditivity of S; strict discriminant descent at walls. I verified the quadratic identities (5.?) symbolically with sympy (both residuals are 0).
sibling_notes: The family-055 board was empty when I started; I posted my summary. Observation: the Θ=1 construction and the heart identification in Secs 6–7 seem to use K_X ≃ O_X only to write down the Todd correction γ. Lifting td(X)^{-1} works the same way in general, so the hypothesis looks stronger than the argument needs. This is not an error.
